audit.whatIsWrong: whys[1] and whys[2] contradict their own rows. win[1] and win[2] give Levels 2 and 3 to Camille, and spikes[0].text plus early both call 2-3 'your cleanest window' - but whys[1] says his heal 'refunds your level-2 poke faster than your trade lands, so he edges the early short-trade exchange' and whys[2] says level 3 tilts 'his way'.
audit.why: 50.16% over 626 games is the headline, and the rest of the file is consistent: Camille's Q-recast true damage and Tactical Sweep's outer edge beat a pre-item Mordekaiser, which is why the chart gives her 2 and 3. The whys are the outliers.
audit.corrected: Rewrote whys[1] and whys[2] to agree with their rows and with the rest of the matchup, keeping the sides and ratings untouched.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown appears in the whole matchup, so 'confirm his R is on cooldown', 'sidestep the telegraphed E pull' and 'peel out before Indestructible heals it back' are all instructions without clocks.
audit.why: Obliterate 8/7/6/5/4s, Indestructible 12/11/10/9/8s, Death's Grasp 16/14/12/10/8s, Realm of Death 140/120/100s. The 140s on his R at rank 1 is what makes 'trade after his ult' a real plan rather than a hope.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text, early, mid and late now carry Indestructible's 12s, Death's Grasp's 16s and Realm of Death's 140s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The interaction that decides every trade is absent: Indestructible builds its shield from damage he DEALS AND TAKES, so your own burst is what pays for the shield he then converts to health. The page treats it as a flat heal on a timer. Darkness Rise (P) is also never mentioned - it only switches on after three hits land, which is exactly the number your short trades should stay under. There is no Grievous Wounds call anywhere. Camille's passive is spelled 'Adaptive Defense' twice; it is Adaptive Defenses. Hookshot is called a stun; Riot says knock-up.
audit.why: Riot, Indestructible: 'Mordekaiser stores damage he deals and takes to create a shield. He may consume the shield to heal.' Darkness Rise: 'Mordekaiser gains a powerful damage aura and Move Speed after landing 3 attacks or spells against champions or monsters.' _missing-interactions.json flags needs-antiheal on Indestructible for this pairing.
audit.corrected: early, mid, late, whys[1] and whys[2] now say the shield is fed by your own damage, cap the exchange under three of his hits, and buy Grievous Wounds before the conversion decides the lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal anywhere, in the one matchup on the list where a heal is named as the reason each stage flips.
audit.why: Indestructible is his entire sustain plan on a 12s cooldown at rank 1, and the page's own late section says you win by bursting 'before Indestructible converts it back'. Grievous Wounds is that plan.
audit.corrected: late now names the Grievous Wounds timing against the conversion.

edits.before: His Indestructible heal refunds your level-2 poke faster than your trade lands, so he edges the early short-trade exchange.
edits.after: Level 2 is yours: the empowered Q plus its true-damage recast lands before Indestructible has stored enough of your damage to matter.

edits.before: Once Indestructible is online he out-sustains your Q-recast trades and his Q punishes any isolated step-up, tilting level 3 his way.
edits.after: With W online your outer-edge max-HP slash and the Q recast out-trade him — break off under three of his hits so Darkness Rise never switches on.

edits.before: Both of you are weak level 1 with one ability — your Adaptive Defense shield eats his Q or auto and trades evenly, so neither owns it; farm and proc the shield.
edits.after: Both of you are weak level 1 with one ability — your Adaptive Defenses shield eats his Q or auto and trades evenly, so neither owns it; farm and proc the shield.

edits.before: Morde's first AP item (Riftmaker/Liandry) plus Indestructible peaks his extended-fight pattern — do not sit in his E-pull range trading autos into an isolated Q slam, or his shield out-heals your whole trade.
edits.after: Morde's first AP item plus Indestructible (12s) peaks his extended-fight pattern — don't sit in Death's Grasp range trading autos into an isolated Q slam, because your own damage is what fills that shield.

edits.before: Stack W's percent-max-HP damage and items to grind through his shield-heal once you reach 2+ items
edits.after: Stack W's percent-max-HP damage and Grievous Wounds to grind through his shield-heal at 2+ items

edits.before: Level 1 is a coinflip neither of you wants to escalate: your Adaptive Defense shield can absorb his first Q or auto, but with one ability each, nobody commits — proc the shield over CS and respect his Indestructible heal. Your cleanest window opens at 2-3: walk up, land the empowered Precision Protocol, wait the beat and re-cast it for the true-damage second hit, then clip him with Tactical Sweep's outer edge for max-HP damage and slow, and peel out with E before Indestructible converts the trade back to health. Stay out of his E range — if Death's Grasp pulls you in, you eat the isolated bonus on his Q and his full kit lands, so trade on YOUR step-up, never his.
edits.after: Level 1 is a coinflip neither of you wants to escalate: your Adaptive Defenses shield can absorb his first Q or auto, but with one ability each nobody commits — proc the shield over CS. Your cleanest window opens at 2-3: land the empowered Precision Protocol, wait the beat and re-cast for the true-damage second hit, then clip him with Tactical Sweep's outer edge and peel out with E. Indestructible (12s) is built from the damage he deals AND takes, so every extra second you stand there is shield you are paying for. Stay out of Death's Grasp (16s) range — if that pull lands you eat the isolated bonus on his Q and his full kit connects, so trade on YOUR step-up, never his, and break off before Darkness Rise gets its third hit.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 tilt to him because Indestructible's shield-heal answers your short trades and his Q punishes any isolated step-up, and at 6 Realm of Death is the single button that beats you — pressed right it locks you in a 1v1, drags a slice of your stats, and turns your dive into his duel. Hold E as a pure escape here, not as engage: the instant you E onto a 6+ Morde you commit to the exact isolated fight his ultimate wants. Keep trading with Q-recast and Tactical Sweep from max range, sidestep the telegraphed E pull, and never flip into him without an exit and without knowing his R timer.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 tilt to him because Indestructible answers your short trades with the damage you just dealt, and at 6 Realm of Death is the single button that beats you — pressed right it locks you in a 1v1, drags a slice of your stats, and turns your dive into his duel. Hold E as a pure escape here, not as engage: the instant you E onto a 6+ Morde you commit to the exact isolated fight his 140s ultimate wants. Keep trading with Q-recast and Tactical Sweep from max range, sidestep the telegraphed E pull, and never flip in without an exit.

edits.before: This is where you flip the lane back. Tactical Sweep deals percent-of-max-HP damage and heals you off him — exactly what chews through Indestructible's shield-and-heal once you have items — and your E mobility lets you kite the dead window after his dash-less R expires. Now look to isolate HIM with Hextech Ultimatum: lock him in your arena, W for the percent-HP shred, and Q-recast for the true damage before Indestructible can convert it back. He has no dash to chase you off, so a clean 2+ item Camille out-skirmishes him — just confirm his R is on cooldown before you commit, since trading ults into a fed Morde still favors him.
edits.after: This is where you flip the lane back. Tactical Sweep deals percent-of-max-HP damage and heals you off him — exactly what chews through Indestructible once you have items and Grievous Wounds to stop the conversion — and your E mobility kites the dead window after his dash-less R expires. Now isolate HIM with Hextech Ultimatum: lock him in your arena, W for the percent-HP shred, Q-recast for the true damage. He has no dash to chase you off, so a clean 2+ item Camille out-skirmishes him — just confirm his 140s R is down before you commit, since trading ults into a fed Morde still favors him even now.

edits.before: Hookshot (E) unlocks your wall-dash stun and attack-speed burst. Only take a wall trade when Mordekaiser's Realm of Death is down, then peel out on the bonus move speed before he answers. Camille is favoured here.
edits.after: Hookshot (E) unlocks your wall-dash knock-up and attack-speed burst. Only take a wall trade when Mordekaiser's Realm of Death is down, then peel out on the bonus move speed before he answers. Camille is favoured here.

edits.before: Good trade: Lead with the W outer edge as Mordekaiser steps to last-hit, weave the empowered Q2 true damage, then peel out on your bonus move speed before the fight goes long. Great trade: Mordekaiser uses or whiffs Realm of Death: instantly E off a wall for the stun and attack-speed surge, Q-recast for the true-damage second hit, W to heal, and R to isolate him if he tries to run. Bad trade: Burning Hookshot (E) aggressively, missing the stun, and getting stuck in a drawn-out melee grind while your E and shield are down. That is how Camille loses a winning lane.

notes: Two whys directly contradicted their own level-chart rows (whys[1] and whys[2] hand levels 2 and 3 to Mordekaiser while win[1]/win[2] and every other string on the page give them to Camille). I rewrote the whys rather than the rows, because spikes[0] and early independently agree that 2-3 is Camille's window. The mechanical find is Indestructible: the shield is stored from damage he DEALS AND TAKES, so the page's advice to stand and trade is literally what funds the heal it then warns you about. Darkness Rise needing three landed hits gives the short-trade rule a number it never had. No Grievous Wounds appeared anywhere in a matchup whose late section says you win by bursting before he converts.
